events.description_en: Work on the Greek Septuagint reportedly began in Egypt in the days of Ptolemy Philadelphus (285-246 B.C.E.), starting with the Pentateuch, traditionally translated by 72 Jewish scholars.

sources.title_en: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time
sources.quote_en: c. 280 B.C.E. The Greek Septuagint begun
Reportedly, work on it commenced in Egypt in the days of Ptolemy Philadelphus (285-246 B.C.E.)
the Septuagint was begun in the third century B.C.E.

events.title_en: Antigonus II Gonatas becomes king of Macedonia
events.description_en: Antigonus II Gonatas, grandson of one of Alexander's generals, ascended the throne of Macedonia.
events.description_ta: பொ.ச.மு. 276-ல் அலெக்ஸாந்தரின் தளபதிகளில் ஒருவரது பேரனான இரண்டாம் ஆன்டிகோனஸ் கானடஸ், மக்கெதோனிய அரியணையில் ஏறினார்.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: Antigonus II Gonatas, grandson of one of Alexander's generals, ascended to the throne of Macedonia in 276 B.C.E.

events.title_en: Antiochus II and Ptolemy II make an 'equitable arrangement'
events.description_en: The king of the north, Antiochus II, and the king of the south, Ptolemy II, made an alliance; Antiochus divorced Laodice and married Ptolemy's daughter Berenice.
events.description_ta: பொ.ச.மு. 250-ல் இந்த இரு ராஜாக்களும் ‘ஒருவரோடொருவர் சம்பந்தம் பண்ணிக்கொண்டார்கள்.’

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: In 250 B.C.E., these two kings entered into 'an equitable arrangement.'

events.title_en: Death of Antiochus II
events.description_en: When Antiochus II died, Berenice did not 'retain the power of her arm.'
events.description_ta: அவர் பொ.ச.மு. 246-ல் இறந்தபோது, பெர்னைஸிக்கு தன் கணவரோடு இருந்த ‘புயபலம் இராமற்போயிற்று.’

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: When he died in 246 B.C.E., she did not 'retain the power of her arm' with her husband.

events.title_en: Seleucus II retreats to Antioch
events.description_en: With only a small remnant of his army, Seleucus II 'went back to his own soil,' retreating to the Syrian capital, Antioch.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: Seleucus II 'went back to his own soil,' retreating to the Syrian capital Antioch in about 242 B.C.E.

events.title_en: Antiochus III marches against Ptolemy IV
events.description_en: In the spring of 217 B.C.E., Antiochus III left Ptolemais and went north 'all the way to his fortress' in Syria after his clash with the king of the south.
events.description_ta: பொ.ச.மு. 217-ன் இளவேனிற்காலத்தில், மூன்றாம் ஆண்டியோகஸ், தாலமேயஸ் நகரை விட்டு வடக்கே சென்று, சிரியாவிலுள்ள தன் ‘அரண்மட்டும் யுத்தங்கலந்து சேர்ந்தான்.’

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: In the spring of 217 B.C.E., Antiochus III left Ptolemaïs and went north, 'all the way to his fortress' in Syria.

events.title_en: Antiochus III takes Sidon and Jerusalem; Judea passes to the Seleucids
events.description_en: After defeating Egypt's General Scopas at Paneas and taking Sidon, Antiochus the Great captured Jerusalem; Judea passed from the Ptolemaic king of the south to the Seleucid king of the north.
events.description_ta: பொ.ச.மு. 198-ல், எருசலேமும் யூதாவும் எகிப்திய தென்றிசை ராஜாவிடமிருந்து சிரியா தேசத்து வடதிசை ராஜாவிடம் கைமாறின.

sources.quote_en: In 198 B.C.E. Antiochus the Great ... captured Jerusalem, and Judea became a dominion of the Seleucid Empire.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: In 198 B.C.E., Jerusalem and Judah passed from domination by the Egyptian king of the south to that of the Syrian king of the north.

events.title_en: Macedonia and Greece fall to the Romans
events.description_en: Macedonia and Greece, one of the four divisions of Alexander's empire, fell to the Romans.

sources.quote_en: Macedonia and Greece ... fell to the Romans in 197 B.C.E.

events.title_en: Antiochus III's daughter marries Ptolemy V
events.description_en: At the marriage of Antiochus III's daughter Cleopatra I to Ptolemy V, the Syrian king did not hand over the promised provinces.
events.description_ta: இருந்தாலும் பொ.ச.மு. 193-ல் திருமணம் நடந்தபோது, சிரியா தேசத்து ராஜா இந்த மாகாணங்களை ஐந்தாம் தாலமிக்கு தரவில்லை.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: At the marriage in 193 B.C.E., however, the Syrian king did not let these provinces go to Ptolemy V.

events.title_en: War in Greece draws in Antiochus III
events.description_en: A war broke out in Greece, and Antiochus III was induced to come there, bringing him into conflict with Rome.
events.description_ta: பொ.ச.மு. 192-ல் கிரீஸில் ஒரு யுத்தம் மூண்டது, இதனால் மூன்றாம் ஆண்டியோகஸ் கிரீஸுக்கு வர தூண்டப்பட்டார்.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: A war broke out in Greece in 192 B.C.E., and Antiochus III was induced to come to Greece.

events.title_en: Antiochus III defeated by Rome at Magnesia
events.description_en: After losing the battle of Magnesia, Antiochus III had to give up everything in Greece, Asia Minor, and west of the Taurus Mountains.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: About a year after losing the battle of Magnesia in 190 B.C.E., he had to give up everything in Greece, Asia Minor

events.title_en: Death of Antiochus III
events.description_en: Antiochus III died while trying to rob a temple at Elymais, Persia.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: Antiochus III died while trying to rob a temple at Elymaïs, Persia, in 187 B.C.E.

events.title_en: High priest Onias deposed by Antiochus Epiphanes
events.description_en: Antiochus IV Epiphanes deposed the Jewish high priest Onias; some Jewish commentators wrongly applied Daniel 9:26 to him.

sources.quote_en: a high priest, Onias, who was deposed by Antiochus Epiphanes in 175 B.C.E.

events.title_en: Antiochus IV humiliated by Rome; Macedonia defeated
events.description_en: Antiochus IV complied with Roman demands to withdraw from Egypt and returned to Syria; the same year Rome again defeated Macedonia.
events.description_ta: பொ.ச.மு. 168-ல் அவர் சிரியாவுக்குத் திரும்புகிறார்.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 14
sources.quote_en: Humiliated, Antiochus IV complies with Roman demands and returns to Syria in 168 B.C.E.
Macedonia warred against the Romans but was again defeated in 168 B.C.E.

events.title_en: Antiochus IV desecrates the temple
events.description_en: Seeking to Hellenize the Jews, Antiochus IV Epiphanes dedicated Jerusalem's temple to Zeus, built an altar on the great altar, and sacrificed swine there. This led to the Maccabean (Hasmonaean) revolt.
events.description_ta: பொ.ச.மு. 167 டிசம்பரில், ஆலய பிரகாரத்தில் புறமத கடவுளுக்கு பலிபீடம் அமைக்கப்பட்டது.

sources.quote_en: On this occasion (Chislev 25, 168 B.C.E.) ... Antiochus sacrificed swine on the altar
This led to the Maccabean (or Hasmonaean) revolt.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: In December 167 B.C.E., a pagan altar was erected on top of the great altar

images.caption_en: Zeus. The Greek gods had human form and often were viewed as grossly immoral

conflicts.note: dp ch. 13 dates the pagan altar to December 167 B.C.E.; Insight 'Festival of Dedication', 'Jerusalem', 'Greece' and 'Temple' give 168 B.C.E. (Chislev 25). Insight value used as primary.

events.notes: display_ta/description_ta are from dp Tamil, which uses 167 (see conflicts).

events.title_en: Judas Maccabaeus rededicates the temple; Festival of Dedication
events.title_ta: கிரேக்க விக்கிரகாராதனையால் தீட்டுப்படுத்தப்பட்டபின் ஆலய மறுபிரதிஷ்டை; பிரதிஷ்டை பண்டிகை
events.description_en: After a three-year struggle, Judas Maccabaeus recaptured the city and temple, built a new altar, and rededicated it on Chislev 25, exactly three years after its profanation; the eight-day Festival of Dedication commemorates it.

sources.title_en: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time
sources.quote_en: 165 B.C.E. Rededication of temple after desecration by Greek idolatry; Festival of Dedication
the rededication took place on Chislev 25, 165 B.C.E., exactly three years to the day

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: In 164 B.C.E., on the anniversary of the desecration, Judas Maccabaeus rededicated the temple

conflicts.note: dp ch. 13 dates the rededication to 164 B.C.E.; si and Insight give Chislev 25, 165 B.C.E.

events.title_en: Death of Antiochus IV
events.description_en: Antiochus IV died in 163 B.C.E.; later Seleucid kings did not occupy the position of 'the king of the north.'

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 14
sources.quote_en: even though other kings of the Seleucid dynasty rule Syria after Antiochus IV dies in 163 B.C.E.

events.title_en: Maccabean Jews appeal to Rome
events.description_en: With the war against the Seleucids continuing, the Jews appealed to Rome for help, bringing Roman influence onto the Jerusalem scene.

sources.quote_en: The Jews appealed to Rome for help and thus a new power came on the Jerusalem scene in about 160 B.C.E.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: The Maccabees probably made a treaty with Rome in 161 B.C.E.

conflicts.note: dp ch. 13 says the Maccabees probably made a treaty with Rome in 161 B.C.E.

events.title_en: Septuagint translation completed
events.description_en: Translation of the entire Hebrew Scriptures into Greek was finally completed during the second century B.C.E., perhaps by 150 B.C.E.

sources.quote_en: translation of the entire Hebrew Scriptures had finally been completed during the second century B.C.E. and perhaps by 150 B.C.E.

events.title_en: Rome destroys Corinth; Achaia and Macedonia become provinces
events.description_en: After the Achaean League rebelled, Rome's armies destroyed Corinth and formed the province of Achaia; Macedonia also became a Roman province.
events.description_ta: காலப்போக்கில் மக்கெதோனியா ரோமைச் சார்ந்திருக்கலாயிற்று, இறுதியாக பொ.ச.மு. 146-ல் ரோமோடு இணைந்துவிட்டது.

sources.quote_en: Led by Corinth, the Achaean League rebelled in 146 B.C.E., and Rome's armies marched into southern Greece and destroyed Corinth.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: ended up as a Roman province in 146 B.C.E.

events.title_en: Simon Maccabaeus makes Jerusalem capital of a free region
events.description_en: Simon Maccabaeus made Jerusalem the capital of a region ostensibly free from subservience or taxation to Gentile nations.

sources.quote_en: About 142 B.C.E., Simon Maccabaeus was able to make Jerusalem the capital of a region ostensibly free

events.title_en: John Hyrcanus I forces circumcision on the Idumeans
events.description_en: According to Josephus, the Maccabean ruler John Hyrcanus I subjugated the Idumeans (Edomites) and forced circumcision on them; Herod's family were therefore nominally Jews.

sources.quote_en: the Idumeans had had circumcision forced upon them by the Maccabean ruler John Hyrcanus I in about 125 B.C.E.

events.title_en: Aristobulus I takes the title of king
events.description_en: Aristobulus I, Jerusalem's high priest and not of David's line, assumed the title of king, establishing a Maccabean kingdom.
events.description_ta: 38 மக்கபேயர்கள் பொ.ச.மு. 161-ல் ரோமோடு சமாதான ஒப்பந்தம் செய்து, பொ.ச.மு. 104-ல் ஒரு ராஜ்யத்தை ஏற்படுத்தியிருக்க வேண்டும்.

sources.quote_en: Aristobulus I, Jerusalem's high priest, even assumed the title of king in 104 B.C.E.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: established a kingdom in 104 B.C.E.

events.title_en: Pompey makes Syria a Roman province
events.description_en: Roman General Pompey made Syria a Roman province, ending the Seleucid dynasty.
events.description_ta: இறுதியாக பொ.ச.மு. 64-ல் சிரியா ரோம மாகாணமானது.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: his dynasty ruled until 64 B.C.E. when Roman General Gnaeus Pompey made Syria a Roman province.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 14

events.title_en: Pompey takes Jerusalem; Rome rules
events.title_ta: ரோம், ஆறாவது உலக வல்லரசு, எருசலேமை ஆளுகிறது
events.description_en: Called in to settle the quarrel between Aristobulus II and Hyrcanus, Roman forces under Pompey besieged Jerusalem for three months and took it; Rome, the sixth world power, now ruled Jerusalem.
events.description_ta: பொ.ச.மு. 63-ல் ரோம தளபதியான நேயஸ் பாம்பி, எருசலேமை மூன்று மாதம் முற்றுகையிட்டுக் கைப்பற்றினார்.

sources.title_en: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time
sources.quote_en: 63 B.C.E. Rome, sixth world power, rules Jerusalem
Under General Pompey, Roman forces besieged Jerusalem in 63 B.C.E.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: The Roman General Gnaeus Pompey took Jerusalem in 63 B.C.E. after a three-month siege.
Pompey, upon conquering Jerusalem in 63 B.C.E., took Jews to Rome as slaves.

conflicts.note: dp chs. 4, 9, 10 date Rome as world power 'from 30 B.C.E.' (fall of Ptolemaic Egypt); si says Rome rules Jerusalem from 63 B.C.E. Different reference points.

events.title_en: Julius Caesar invades Britannia
events.description_en: Roman General Julius Caesar invaded Britannia but failed to establish a permanent settlement.
events.description_ta: பொ.ச.மு. 55-ல் ரோம தளபதி ஜூலியஸ் சீசர் பிரிட்டானியாமீது படையெடுத்தார், ஆனால் அவரால் ஒரு நிரந்தரமான குடியிருப்பை ஏற்படுத்த முடியவில்லை.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 9
sources.quote_en: In 55 B.C.E., Roman General Julius Caesar invaded Britannia but failed to establish a permanent settlement.

events.title_en: Lex Julia majestatis enacted
events.description_en: The law called lex Julia majestatis made it an offense to engage in any activity against the sovereign power of Rome, a background to the charges later brought against Jesus.

sources.quote_en: In 48 B.C.E., the law called lex Julia majestatis had made it an offense to engage in any activity against the sovereign power of Rome.

events.title_en: Herod made governor of Galilee
events.description_en: Antipater II appointed his son Herod governor of Galilee, where Herod distinguished himself by ridding the territory of robber bands.

sources.quote_en: the time Herod received his appointment as governor of Galilee (which is generally dated 47 B.C.E.)

events.title_en: Julius Caesar appointed dictator
events.description_en: Gaius Julius Caesar was appointed dictator of Rome for ten years.

sources.quote_en: In 46 B.C.E., Gaius Julius Caesar was appointed dictator of Rome for ten years

events.title_en: Julius Caesar assassinated
events.description_en: Julius Caesar was murdered by conspirators; his great-nephew Octavian was then only 18.
events.description_ta: பொ.ச.மு. 44-ல் ஜூலியஸ் சீசர் கொலைசெய்யப்பட்ட போது, அவரது சகோதரியின் பேரனான கயஸ் ஆக்டேவியனுக்கு 18 வயதுதான்.

sources.quote_en: but he was murdered in 44 B.C.E.
murdered by conspirators in 44 B.C.E.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 14
sources.quote_en: In 44 B.C.E. when Julius Caesar was assassinated, his sister's grandson Gaius Octavian was only 18 years of age.

events.title_en: Herod appointed king of Judea by the Roman Senate
events.description_en: On Mark Antony's recommendation, the Roman senate appointed the Edomite Herod king of greater Judea, though he could not establish himself in Jerusalem until about three years later.
events.description_ta: பொ.ச.மு. 39-ல், ரோம பேரவை ஏதோமியரான ஏரோதை யூதேயாவின் ராஜாவாக்கியது.

sources.quote_en: about 39 B.C.E., was made king of greater Judea by appointment of the Roman senate

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: In 39 B.C.E., the Roman Senate appointed Herod—an Edomite—to be king of Judea.

images.caption_en: Ruins of multileveled palace built by Herod the Great atop Masada

conflicts.note: Insight 'Herod' notes Josephus' method would place the appointment in 40 B.C.E., while Appianos' data place it in 39 B.C.E.

events.title_en: Herod takes Jerusalem by storm
events.title_ta: ஏரோது (ரோம் நியமித்த அரசன்) மூர்க்கத் தாக்குதலால் எருசலேமைக் கைப்பற்றுகிறார்
events.description_en: Herod, appointed king by Rome, took Jerusalem and deposed Antigonus, ending Maccabean rule; his rule effectively began from this date.
events.description_ta: பொ.ச.மு. 37-ல் எருசலேமை இவர் கைப்பற்றவே, மக்கபேயர்களின் ஆட்சி முடிவுக்கு வந்தது.

sources.title_en: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time
sources.quote_en: c. 37 B.C.E. Herod (appointed king by Rome) takes Jerusalem by storm

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: Ending the Maccabean rule, he took Jerusalem in 37 B.C.E.
He did not get control of Jerusalem until 37 or 36 B.C.E., from which date his rule effectively began.

conflicts.note: Insight 'Herod' notes Josephus also says it was 27 years after Pompey's capture (63), which would make it 36 B.C.E.; Insight 'Jerusalem' says '37 or 36'.

events.title_en: Octavian defeats Antony and Cleopatra at Actium
events.description_en: At the battle of Actium, Octavian defeated the combined forces of Cleopatra VII and Mark Antony and emerged as the undisputed ruler of the Roman Empire.
events.description_ta: (தானியேல் 11:14) பொ.ச.மு. 31-ல், ஆக்டியம் யுத்தத்தின்போது, தாலமிய வம்சத்தின் கடைசி ராணியான ஏழாம் க்ளியோபாட்ரா, அவளது ரோம காதலன் மார்க் ஆன்டனி ஆகிய இருவரது ஒன்றிணைந்த படைகளையும் ரோம அரசரான ஆக்டேவியன் வீழ்த்தினார்.

sources.quote_en: In September, 31 B.C.E. ... Octavius emerged the undisputed ruler of the Roman Empire.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 14
sources.quote_en: During the battle of Actium, in 31 B.C.E., Roman ruler Octavian defeats the combined forces of the last Ptolemaic queen

events.title_en: Ptolemaic Egypt falls to Rome
events.description_en: The Ptolemaic dynasty, last of the four Hellenistic kingdoms, fell to Rome; by 30 B.C.E. Rome had supremacy over Syria and Egypt and emerged as the world power of Bible prophecy.
events.description_ta: தாலமியின் ராஜ வம்சம், பொ.ச.மு. 30-ல் எகிப்தை ரோம் கைப்பற்றியது வரை ஆட்சியில் இருந்தது.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 9
sources.quote_en: The Ptolemaic dynasty continued to rule in Egypt until it fell to Rome in 30 B.C.E.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 14
sources.quote_en: By the year 30 B.C.E., Rome has supremacy over both Syria and Egypt.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 4
sources.title_en: The Rise and Fall of an Immense Image

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 10
sources.title_en: Who Can Stand Against the Prince of Princes?

events.title_en: Octavian given the title Augustus
events.description_en: The Roman Senate bestowed on Octavian the title 'Augustus'; he became the first emperor of Rome, known as Caesar Augustus, whose rule ran from 27 B.C.E. to 14 C.E.
events.description_ta: மேலும், பொ.ச.மு. 27, ஜனவரி 16 அன்று, பேரவை ஆக்டேவியனுக்கு “அகஸ்டஸ்” என்ற பட்டப்பெயர் சூட்டியது.

events.title_en: Province of Achaia includes all southern and central Greece
events.description_en: By 27 B.C.E. the Roman province of Achaia came to include all of southern and central Greece.

sources.quote_en: The province of 'Achaia' was formed and by 27 B.C.E. came to include all of southern and central Greece.

events.title_en: Herod begins rebuilding the temple
events.description_en: According to Josephus, Herod began rebuilding Zerubbabel's temple in the 18th year of his reign, which could mean 18/17 B.C.E. The sanctuary took 18 months and other main structures eight years, but work continued long after.

conflicts.note: Insight 'Temple' notes Josephus' Jewish War says the 15th year, while Jewish Antiquities says the 18th (the generally accepted figure).

events.title_en: Augustus becomes Pontifex Maximus
events.description_en: After the death of Lepidus, Augustus assumed the title 'Pontifex Maximus' (high priest).

sources.quote_en: After the death of Lepidus in 12 B.C.E., Augustus assumed the title 'Pontifex Maximus.'

events.title_en: Birth of John the Baptizer foretold to Zechariah
events.description_en: While priest Zechariah offered incense in the temple sanctuary during the division of Abijah, probably in late spring or early summer of 3 B.C.E., the angel Gabriel foretold the birth of his son John.

events.title_en: Augustus given the title 'Father of His Country'
events.description_en: In 2 B.C.E., the year of Jesus' birth, the Roman Senate gave Augustus the title Pater Patriae.

events.title_en: Death of Herod the Great
events.description_en: Bible chronology, astronomical data, and historical records point to 1 B.C.E. (or possibly early 1 C.E.) for Herod's death, shortly after his decree to kill Bethlehem's babes; a total lunar eclipse occurred on January 8, 1 B.C.E.

sources.quote_en: The available evidence indicates that Herod died likely in the year 1 B.C.E.
there is evidence pointing to the year 1 B.C.E. as the likely time of his death.
Herod died, evidently in the year 1 B.C.E.

conflicts.note: Insight notes some chronologers hold 5 or 4 B.C.E. based on the partial eclipse of March 11, 4 B.C.E.; jw.org favors 1 B.C.E.
